title: Edge audit ingress: proxy sharding, retransmit policy, and loss-detection hooks
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement an edge-side audit-ingress proxy design that shards tenant traffic, maintains ordered delivery semantics per-tenant where required, surfaces loss-detection hooks for downstream retransmit, and provides end-to-end observability for SIEM/webhook consumers (Splunk/Datadog). This ticket focuses on protocol and runtime guarantees for ingress plus operator-facing traces and metrics.
background: Customers and internal teams expect near-exact delivery guarantees for audit streams sent to external SIEMs. Current forwarders occasionally surface transient drops during edge restarts and burst overloads; downstream partners see duplicates or gaps and open support tickets. Existing efforts focused on webhook retries and DLQs at the forwarder level, but we've lacked a cohesive edge sharding + loss-detection model that scales across tenants and supports different delivery semantics (at-least-once, best-effort, ordered per-tenant).
acceptance_criteria: Edge ingress proxy accepts audit events and assigns stable shard keys per tenant so downstream forwarders can preserve ordering or parallelize safely
A retransmit protocol exists: edge maintains short-term buffer + sequence watermarks and exposes a /retransmit API for downstream connectors to request missing ranges
Loss-detection hooks implemented: per-tenant sequence monotonic check emits 'gap' events to observability and triggers configurable retransmit policies
End-to-end tracing: request IDs propagated through edge -> forwarder -> external webhook, viewable in Console tracing tab
Metrics: per-shard depth, retransmit requests, gap rate, duplicate rate, and reorder rate emitted to datadog with tags {tenant, region, shard, delivery_tier}
Backpressure: proxy applies token-bucket per-tenant with configurable soft/hard limits and reports throttle decisions to Console
Automated integration smoke test validating retransmit and ordering for Splunk HEC and Datadog webhook adapters completes in CI
tasks: Design shard assignment algorithm (consistent hashing vs tenant-affinity) and write proposal
Prototype edge buffer with sequence watermark store (in-memory with optional Redis fallback)
Define retransmit REST contract and authentication for forwarders
Instrument tracing propagation and add Console trace view link
Add Datadog/Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboard templates
Create end-to-end CI test harness that simulates edge restart, message loss, and retransmit scenarios
Update runbook with operational thresholds and remediation steps
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Kickoff meeting held with Security, Infra, and Integrations SMEs. Decision to prioritize at-least-once with optional ordered mode per-tenant.
2025-02-24: Prototype of in-memory buffer complete; initial benchmark shows 10ms median retention latency for 100K TPS across 64 shards.
2025-03-01: Retransmit API v1 spec drafted; opted for short-lived tokens tied to tenant API keys with scoped RBAC checks. Shared in #integrations for feedback.
2025-03-05: Implemented gap detection and emitted 'audit:gap-detected' telemetry. Observability team validated tags schema. Started work on CI harness.
decisions: Use per-tenant shard assignment via consistent hashing seeded by tenant_id and region to provide stable routing while allowing rebalancing
Retransmit tokens will be time-limited (default 10m) and signed using existing KMS service to avoid stateful long-term token storage on edge
Support two delivery modes: 'ordered' (per-tenant sequence preserved, potential higher tail latency) and 'parallel' (higher throughput, no per-tenant ordering guarantees).
Don't attempt full exactly-once semantics; instead provide deterministic dedupe tokens for forwarders to use when idempotency is required by destination
Keep initial buffer in memory with a Redis fallback for tenants requesting extended retransmit windows; evaluate persistence cost if adoption grows
